title: Inclusion between c.e. sets is Pi2-complete, not Sigma2-complete.
details: Marks, version2024-02-25, Exercise17.6, printed/PDF p.72, visually confirmed: {(d,e): W_d is a subset of W_e} is asserted Sigma2-complete. It is Pi2-complete. Using computable stages, inclusion is equivalent to forall x,s exists t [x not in W_d,s or x in W_e,t], a Pi2 formula after tuple coding. Fix an index u with W_u=N. Then e maps computably to (u,e), and W_u subset W_e iff W_e=N iff phi_e is total. Proposition17.4 therefore gives Pi2-hardness. Properness of the hierarchy rules out the asserted Sigma2 classification. Replace Sigma2 by Pi2. This adjacent exercise is excluded from the selected TOT/FIN/INF entry and has no current consuming entry. Current adoption2026-11-09: the domain-comparison entry proves the Pi2 normal form and explicit totality reduction; it adopts the correction.
